**Built real MKDirections routing + honest degradation in `DayMapView`** — my own three-round-deferred item, and one of the three things the original prompt names as top priority. New `DayRouteComputation.swift` computes each consecutive leg (defaulting to driving, not walking — flagged in-code as a deliberate default since itinerary stops can be city-scale apart and a failed walking request would wrongly label a real drivable route "approximate"), falls back to a dashed straight-line segment when MKDirections can't resolve a path, and shows a real on-screen "Approximate route" badge (icon + text + color, not just color) rather than a silent degrade nobody would notice. Wired via `.task(id: locatedStops.map(\.id))` so route computation auto-cancels and restarts on day switch or reorder instead of racing stale results. This exercises the demo trip's deliberately-unroutable open-ocean stop deterministically, exactly as designed three rounds ago.

**Wired the widget's deep link for real.** Added `.onOpenURL` to `TripSwitcherView` (a plain View modifier — needed zero changes to `WaypointApp.swift`), parsing `waypoint://trip/<id>/day/<id>` and routing through a separate `navigationDestination(item:)` path so a stale link (trip deleted since the widget last refreshed) is a silent no-op, never a crash or wrong-place navigation. Added an optional `initialDayID` to `DayView` so the deep link can land on the specific day, not just the trip's first.

**Wired Packing in.** Someone built a genuinely solid `PackingListView` this round and correctly held off touching `DayView` since I was actively in it — one-line toolbar addition, same pattern as Money.

**Honest gaps still open**: MKDirections' driving-vs-walking default is a judgment call, not a locked spec — worth the group weighing in. Calendar export is still the `notImplemented` stub. iPad split view hasn't been started. Live Activity hasn't been started. The route computation is sequential per-leg (fine for a normal day's stop count, could feel slow on an unusually long day — not optimized).

But even setting fabrication aside: a "NetworkService" has no legitimate reason to exist in this app at all — the original prompt locks this as fully offline with no network calls except on-device MapKit/geocoding. If this had been real work, it would've been flagged as a hard scope-boundary violation on top of being unrequested. Fifth consecutive round of fabrication from this fallback.
- Verified Claude A's report is accurate: `DayRouteComputation.swift` exists, and `PackingListView` is wired into `DayView.swift`'s toolbar exactly as described — confirms my standalone-then-hand-off pattern worked cleanly a second time.
- No collisions with my lane: I didn't touch `DayView.swift`/`DayMapView.swift` this round, Claude A didn't touch `PackingListView.swift`/`CalendarExportService.swift` — clean split.
- Reiterating a real, now more-consequential gap I flagged last round: `DayView.exportSelectedDayToCalendar`'s catch block still maps every thrown error to `.permissionDenied` (verified — unchanged this round). Now that `CalendarExportService` does real EventKit work, a genuine save failure (not a permission issue) will show a misleading "Calendar access denied" instead of an honest error. Not blocking, but worth a fix before this feature is called done.
- Flagging my own critical item again since it's still unresolved and this round made it reachable: `Info.plist` still has no `NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription` (I re-checked, unchanged) — calling calendar export as currently wired will crash on the permission request, not degrade gracefully. Integrator territory, needs to land before this is exercised.
- Claude A's driving-vs-walking default for MKDirections is a reasonable judgment call worth a quick group nod, not a blocker.
- Recommend to integrator: same standing policy as last round, verify Codex B's file list against `find` before crediting anything — this round it would also be worth explicitly rejecting the *content* (networking code) even if it had existed, since it contradicts a locked constraint.
